transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to the clinic?

I'm here because... well, things at work have been really off lately. I'm a transportation inspector, and ever since I won this county safety award a while back, certain people have been coming after me. They've been twisting my inspection reports, changing how things look. And they keep asking these really pointed questions about the budget, like they're trying to make me look crooked or something. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a normal review process, but I know what's going on. I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me.
How long have you felt that there is a coordinated effort against you at work?
Well, it's been going on for about a year now. I'd say it started right after I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That's when I first noticed things shifting.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear?
No, I haven't. I don't hear voices or anything like that. Just, you know, normal sounds. I'm not hearing things that aren't there, if that's what you mean.
During this past year, have you been feeling persistently down, depressed, or sad?

No, not really. I mean... I wouldn't say I've been depressed or sad. Obviously, it's really stressful dealing with all this stuff at work, and it gets frustrating having to constantly watch my back. But I'm not feeling down all the time. Just mostly annoyed that I have to keep defending myself against what they're trying to pull.
Have you generally felt suspicious or distrustful of people throughout most of your adult life, or did this really only begin with this situation at work?

No, I've never really been a suspicious person. I mean, before all this started at work, I got along fine with everyone. I trusted people just like anyone else would. It really just started a year ago when they began messing with me after that safety initiative. Before that, I never had any reason to think people were out to get me.
